title: Extract Email Domain Using SPLIT_PART
description:
Extract the domain part of each user's email address (the part after the `@` sign) using SPLIT_PART.

**Table: users** — `id`, `name`, `email`

Output columns: `name`, `email`, `domain`. Order by `domain`, `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com'),(2,'Bob','bob@gmail.com'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com'),(4,'Dave','dave@yahoo.com'),(5,'Eve','eve@company.org'),(6,'Frank','frank@gmail.com'),(7,'Grace','grace@company.org'),(8,'Henry','henry@yahoo.com');
solution_sql: SELECT name, email, SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2) AS domain FROM users ORDER BY domain, name

test_cases.description: 8 users; domains are company.org (2), example.com (2), gmail.com (2), yahoo.com (2)

hints: SPLIT_PART(string, delimiter, index) splits the string by the delimiter and returns the part at the given 1-based index.
SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2) splits on '@' and returns the second part — the domain.
explanation: SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2) splits each email on '@' and returns the second segment. 'alice@example.com' → ['alice', 'example.com'] → 'example.com'. This is equivalent to SUBSTRING_INDEX(email, '@', -1) in MySQL. All 8 rows are returned with their extracted domain.
